poem_stanzas:
Within the throat a hollow bridge is strung,
Two folded cords that quiver when I speak,
I shelter breath before it becomes song,
And close to guard the road that food must take.

When a cold descends, my gates grow rough and sore,
A whisper cracks where once a trumpet rang,
I am the singer's hidden, hinged door,
The reed the air must pass to find a name.
ciphers.hint: The voice box perched at the top of the windpipe.

poem_stanzas:
Deep in the hardest chambers I reside,
A soft and fatty treasure none can see,
I brew the blood that floods the body's tide,
And nurse the cells that make a remedy.

An oxtail stew once coaxed me to the spoon,
A proverb says I reach down to the bone,
In winter I am warmth, and hunger soon
Will crack me from my cage to feed its own.
ciphers.hint: The soft core hidden inside your largest bones.

poem_stanzas:
I am a quiet workshop small and sealed,
That drips a potent drop into the blood,
No pipe of mine is seen, no door revealed,
Yet messages I send like hidden flood.

Some of me weep upon the skin in heat,
Some sit beneath the jaw and swell with ill,
I answer signals with a silent beat,
A chemical whisper bent to body's will.
ciphers.hint: A tiny organ that pours out hormones or sweat.

poem_stanzas:
Two sisters of a cord share one broad band,
They ride the upper limb and pull it in,
When I am flexed you see a rounded land,
A knot of power that protects from sin.

Heaving and hoisting loads is my employ,
The boxer's coiled spring, the rower's friend,
I shorten, and the forearm swings with joy,
Then lengthen slow to let the labor end.
ciphers.hint: The two-headed muscle you flex to show strength.

poem_stanzas:
A cradle made of bone, a bowl, a ring,
That carries soft and heavy things above,
Two wings that meet and hold the weight of spring,
A gate through which new life must learn to move.

Among the skeleton I am the floor,
The lower ribs descend to find my rim,
I bear the trunk and steady it the more,
And cup the organs at the body's brim.
ciphers.hint: The basin of bone that holds the lower organs.

poem_stanzas:
Between the knee and ankle I stand guard,
The bone that fronts the leg and takes the blow,
I wear no muscle where the skin is hard,
And sting for days when tables catch me low.

I am the part you rub when you have tripped,
The striker's bruise, the child's first scrape and tear,
Down to the foot my slender length is slipped,
The bare and bony edge that stands so near.
ciphers.hint: The front of the lower leg, easy to bark.

poem_stanzas:
I face the ground and never see the sky,
I bear your weight and print a shape in sand,
With every step I flatten, then I rise,
The lowest floor of any standing land.

A cobbler works on me with thread and awl,
I thin where heels grind hardest on the street,
I hold a pebble like a bitter ball,
The tender map of everywhere you meet.
ciphers.hint: The flat underside of your foot.

poem_stanzas:
Above the skull a living carpet grows,
That sheds and bristles, pale or dark or grey,
The barber tends me where the crown wind blows,
And hats and helmets rest on me all day.

I prickle when a whisper names a fright,
I blush beneath the sun and burn to red,
I am the first to silver into white,
The stretch that holds the forest on your head.
ciphers.hint: The skin and hair covering the top of your head.

poem_stanzas:
I am long and lean and made to enter holes,
A musky hunter with a pointed face,
My coat is cream, my nose is black, and all
My joy is threading tunnels I can trace.

A hunter once would send me down a burrow,
I flush the frightened creature from its den,
Domestic now, I coil and sleep and borrow
The sleeves and drawers and human hands again.
ciphers.hint: A slim, fierce hunter once used to chase rabbits.

poem_stanzas:
Upon one island only do I swing,
A ring-tailed climber with a fox's face,
My eyes are round and bright, my fingers cling,
I leap the forest with a ghostly grace.

I bask with arms thrown wide to catch the sun,
My scent is musk, my call a wailing cry,
When night descends my waking has begun,
A stranger swinging through a southern sky.
ciphers.hint: A wide-eyed primate with a long tail, found only on one island.

poem_stanzas:
A forest cat with tassels on my ears,
A stub for tail, a coat of dappled grey,
I pad on silent feet through snowy years,
And see the hare before it turns to flee.

My eyes are wide and amber in the dark,
My beard hangs long and white beneath my chin,
The northern wood is where I leave my mark,
A tufted, silent hunter, lean and thin.
ciphers.hint: A wild cat with tufted ears and a very short tail.

poem_stanzas:
A tawny ghost that haunts the western hills,
A lion's cousin with an unknown name,
I leap the canyon where the cold air spills,
And stalk the deer with neither sound nor flame.

Alone I range, a shadow in the scrub,
No pride to keep me company at night,
I claim a ridge and hunt and sleep and rub
My flanks on bark to mark my hard-won right.
ciphers.hint: A large tawny cat also called a cougar or mountain lion.

poem_stanzas:
Upon a ceiling I can walk at ease,
My padded toes grip glass and plaster wall,
I drop my tail to buy my life when seized,
And it returns, though shorter after all.

My eyes are huge and lidless, always wet,
I chirp a little answer in the night,
A household friend for those who do not fret,
I chase the mosquito in the lamp's warm light.
ciphers.hint: A small lizard that climbs smooth walls with sticky toes.

poem_stanzas:
A spiny dragon of the tropics, I
Bask on a branch and wear a crest of scales,
My dewlap hangs, my whip-like tail can fly,
And green as leaves I hide from searching eyes.

When danger comes I dive into the stream,
A swimmer when I must, though born to climb,
I eat the flowers of the forest's dream,
And grow from small to armored over time.
ciphers.hint: A big crested lizard that lives in tropical treetops.

poem_stanzas:
We live in towns beneath the dusty sand,
And one of us must always stand and stare,
Upright on hind legs like a tiny man,
To watch the sky for wings that hunt from air.

If hawks appear, a whistle starts the rush,
We pour into the tunnels of our home,
Sunbathing in a huddle, warm and lush,
When cold mornings the desert turn to stone.
ciphers.hint: A small burrowing mammal that stands sentinel in the desert.

poem_stanzas:
Nocturnal, stout, and built down near the ground,
I dig a den with front teeth like a spade,
My pouch faces backward so no dirt is found
Within, and all my tunnels I have made.

Among the gum trees of the south I roam,
My droppings come out cubed and neat and square,
A slow and stubborn master of my home,
With powerful claws and coarse and dusty hair.
ciphers.hint: A stocky Australian digger that leaves cube-shaped droppings.

poem_stanzas:
A plump and speckled wanderer of fields,
I run on foot and seldom take to wing,
My body crouched, my feathers are my shields,
I bob and whistle when the mornings sing.

A covey of my kin will rise at once,
Exploding from the stubble in a blur,
We scatter, then regroup among the stems,
And fold again as quiet as we were.
ciphers.hint: A small plump ground bird that bobs its head as it walks.

poem_stanzas:
A little singer of the garden hedge,
My beak is thick to crack the hardest seed,
I flit in yellow, red, or brown, and edge
The feeder where the other birds will feed.

My trills are short and cheerful in the thorn,
I build a cup of grass and moss and hair,
And when the winter strips the field of corn,
I find a feeder hung in city air.
ciphers.hint: A small seed-eating songbird with a stout beak.

poem_stanzas:
I rise on quivering wings above the field,
And sing the higher that I climb the blue,
A speck of morning, hidden and revealed,
A shower of music falling down to you.

To wake before the sun and mount the sky,
To pour a fountain from a burning throat,
Is joy enough; I need no reason why,
I am the morning's own ascending note.
ciphers.hint: A brown bird famous for singing while soaring high.

poem_stanzas:
Upon a chimney I have built my nest,
On legs like stilts I wade the shallow mere,
With clapping bill I greet my mate and rest,
And fly on wings that carry far and clear.

A legend says I bring the newborn down,
A bundle dangling from a crimson beak,
I stand in fields of frogs beyond the town,
And winter drives me south for months to seek.
ciphers.hint: A tall long-legged bird said to deliver babies.

poem_stanzas:
A grey and stately dancer of the marsh,
I bugle with a trumpet in my throat,
On folded wings I rise, and winters harsh
I flee on high for warmer lands remote.

On one leg I may stand the whole night through,
My courtship is a leaping, bowing dance,
A folded bird in paper, inked and true,
That hangs above a sickroom's quiet glance.
ciphers.hint: A tall stately bird that dances and trumpets its call.

poem_stanzas:
Upon the water I am a floating boat,
My bill a basket scooped to hold the sea,
I drain the brine and swallow what will float,
And share the catch with nestlings under me.

On posts and piers I stand with folded wings,
A pale and solemn sentinel of shore,
My hanging pouch is full when fishing brings
A crowd of silver wriggling in its store.
ciphers.hint: A big waterbird with a huge throat pouch for scooping fish.

poem_stanzas:
Upon one slender leg I stand and wade,
My curving neck descends in shallows gray,
The brine I sieve has dyed me where I feed,
And turned my feathers into flushed display.

In crowds of thousands I am seen to dance,
I bow and flag my wings to win a mate,
My courtship is a ballet at a glance,
And colonies of rose await my fate.
ciphers.hint: A wading bird that stands on one leg and turns pink from its food.

poem_stanzas:
I bear a bill too huge to seem my own,
A painted blade of orange, black and gold,
It stretches past my eye, a boastful bone,
And sifts the jungle fruit my branches hold.

My forest rings with croaks and clacks and trills,
I nest within a hollow in a tree,
A flash of color in the wooded hills,
A bird the size of mischief, bold and free.
ciphers.hint: A tropical bird with an enormous colorful bill.

poem_stanzas:
I cling to branches with a grip of two,
And nap for hours while the sun is high,
My diet is a gum-leaf, tough to chew,
Across the treetops I am slow to fly.

My nose is broad and black, my coat is grey,
My pouch is slung to hold my baby near,
I climb where fragrant branches bend and sway,
And munch a bitter leaf through all the year.
ciphers.hint: A sleepy Australian tree-dweller that eats eucalyptus leaves.

poem_stanzas:
I hang beneath a branch with hooking claws,
And move so slowly moss will grow on fur,
For weeks I drowse and break no forest laws,
And rarely hurry, rarely even stir.

I climb down only when I need to go,
A single errand, then I climb again,
My motions are a minute, soft and slow,
And patience is the measure of my den.
ciphers.hint: A slow tree-hanging mammal of the American tropics.

poem_stanzas:
A shaggy ox upon the roof of earth,
My skirt of hair hangs low against the cold,
My horns are curved, my lungs are wide for air,
I chew the mossy grass on mountains old.

Herdsmen will comb my fleece to spin a rope,
And load me as a beast of burden, slow,
I carry milk and butter, fuel and hope,
Across the passes buried deep in snow.
ciphers.hint: A shaggy highland ox of the Himalayas.

poem_stanzas:
I climb the cliffs that others dare not try,
My hooves are pads that grip a ledge of stone,
My horns sweep backward, long and ridged and high,
And winter snows I face and face alone.

The hunter comes to claim my curving crown,
I leap from rock to rock and slip away,
The highest crags are where my kind look down,
The masters of the mountain and the day.
ciphers.hint: A wild mountain goat with long, ridged, backward-curving horns.

poem_stanzas:
A pebble thrown across the dark alone,
A grain of stone that wanders without aim,
I circle with the planets, cold as bone,
Until at last I find the earth's hot flame.

When I descend, my skin begins to glow,
The air will file me down to dust and hiss,
My trail becomes a wishing line below,
A falling star, a momentary kiss.
ciphers.hint: A small rocky body drifting through space before it burns.

poem_stanzas:
A bulging shape that hangs between two states,
Too fat for half, too lean to be a whole,
It swells and ripens while the evening waits,
A lopsided lantern for the owl and vole.

Two nights of this, then it will fill and smile,
Then shrink again through every darkening part,
The sky records each phase and files each mile,
A crescent, then a sliver, then no heart.
ciphers.hint: Describing a moon that is more than half but not fully round.

poem_stanzas:
After the brimming cup has overflowed,
I am the slow retreat, the shrinking edge,
Each evening takes a portion from the road,
Until I hang a lamp on a bent ledge.

I fade toward dark and vanish into none,
A single night of nothing, black and deep,
Then I return the other way, begun
Again to grow while all the world's asleep.
ciphers.hint: The moon's slow shrinking after it has been full.

poem_stanzas:
I am the farthest mark upon a loop,
The widest breath a satellite can draw,
The distant edge where it can slightly droop,
The loneliest point in a celestial law.

Across the ring there waits a closer twin,
Where orbit rushes and the pull is deep,
But I am where the circling slows, and in
That hush the moon and tide may go to sleep.
ciphers.hint: The point in an orbit farthest from the body it circles.

poem_stanzas:
I am the closest brush of any round,
Where circling speed is quickest and most near,
The tightest turn that any moon has wound,
The point where tides on earth begin to rear.

Across the way my distant brother waits,
Where every motion dawdles and is slow,
We are the two extremes of circling fates,
The near and far of every heavenly go.
ciphers.hint: The point in an orbit nearest the body it circles.

poem_stanzas:
Upon the burning face a blemish grows,
A darker island than the blazing sea,
It rises and departs and comes and goes
In cycles that astronomers can see.

I weigh a hundred earths and still I hide
Within the glare that blinds the unaided eye,
I fling a banner down the solar tide,
And paint the polar night with fire on high.
ciphers.hint: A cooler dark patch on the surface of the sun.

poem_stanzas:
A halo of pale fire, a silver mane,
That only shows when day has been undone,
When the black disc devours the shining plain,
And all the birds have fallen silent, stunned.

I reach a million miles into the cold,
A streamer flung from an imprisoned light,
I am the sun's disheveled hair of gold,
That lingers when the sky is torn from night.
ciphers.hint: The pearly outer glow around the sun, seen at an eclipse.

poem_stanzas:
When two great bodies find themselves aligned,
I am the inmost blackness they create,
The cone of purest dark, the deepest blind,
Where light is utterly refused at the gate.

Beside me wanders a paler, looser shade,
A half-lit cousin at the shadow's rim,
I am the core where every sunbeam fled,
The perfect dark at evening's sudden brim.
ciphers.hint: The darkest, central part of a shadow during an eclipse.

poem_stanzas:
I am a tender ache that is not mine,
That blooms when someone else is bowed by pain,
I bring no remedy to lend or sign,
But I will sit beside you in the rain.

I am the sigh before the helping hand,
The knot that tightens at another's fall,
I am the bridge by which the lonely stand,
And mercy is the road I build for all.
ciphers.hint: The tender ache you feel for someone else's suffering.

poem_stanzas:
I come too late, a guest who will not leave,
When deeds are done and cannot be undone,
I sting the memory and make it grieve,
And turn the daylight grey beneath the sun.

I am the conscience with a burning coal,
The echo of a choice no plea can still,
I lodge forever in the guilty soul,
And no forgetting ever breaks my will.
ciphers.hint: The bitter regret for a wrong you have done.

poem_stanzas:
I am the hush before a mountain range,
The widening of the eye beneath the stars,
I make the smallness of a person plain,
And lift the heart above its daily bars.

I come with thunder and with ocean swells,
With newborn life and with the temple's dome,
I am the reverence that silence tells,
The trembling that makes every watcher home.
ciphers.hint: The feeling of wonder and reverence before something vast.

poem_stanzas:
I am the sour seed of small revenge,
That sprouts in one who feels they were denied,
I make a gentle heart turn hard and strange,
And find a bitter pleasure in the pride.

I am the reason pettiness survives,
The pinch of mean delight in another's loss,
I feed on slights and keep the grudge alive,
And nail my grievance to a polished cross.
ciphers.hint: A petty wish to wound or annoy out of resentment.

poem_stanzas:
I am a heavy shadow on the mind,
A grey that gathers when the light has gone,
A mood that makes the kindest world unkind,
And leaves the lonely sitting still till dawn.

I fill the corners of a winter room,
I muffle laughter and I dull the song,
I settle like a mist, a kind of tomb,
And hold the weary quietly too long.
ciphers.hint: A heavy, dark mood or darkness itself.

poem_stanzas:
I am the bubbling that escapes the chest,
The crinkling at the corner of the eyes,
I come when friends and foolish stories best
Unfold, and no one bothers to be wise.

I am the music of a roaring room,
The stamping and the slapping of the knee,
I chase the heavy shadow and its doom,
And leave the heart as light as it can be.
ciphers.hint: Laughter and gladness that spill out in company.

poem_stanzas:
I am the cry beneath the singer's note,
The aching undertow of deep despair,
I am the sorrow that the lonely tote,
The weight of every unanswered prayer.

I am the shadow of a shattered thing,
The far side of a lamentation's sound,
I am the grief that loss and parting bring,
And where I settle, joy is rarely found.
ciphers.hint: Deep sorrow; great trouble.

poem_stanzas:
I am the fire that reason cannot cool,
The burning engine of a chosen cause,
I make a person overstep the rule,
And never stop for comfort or applause.

I am the convert's and the martyr's flame,
The heat that drives the runner through the pain,
The blazing passion that outlives the shame,
The ardor that will labor all in vain.
ciphers.hint: Eager, passionate enthusiasm for a cause.

poem_stanzas:
Beneath the cold and heavy soil I swell,
A bulb that wears a tuft of leafy green,
The farmer pulls me from my earthy cell,
And heaps me in the barn to be unseen.

I am the lantern carved on harvest night,
A root that feeds the cattle through the cold,
A humble harvest for the laborer's bite,
A treasure from the dark and humble mould.
ciphers.hint: A round root vegetable, purple and white, grown in cold fields.

poem_stanzas:
A crimson button buried in the rows,
I ripen quick and crisp and peppery,
My shoulder pokes above, and someone knows
To pull me young, before I grow too free.

On salads I am sliced in rosy rings,
A little pepper-flavored crunch of spring,
I come to tables with the fresh green things,
And make a plainest sandwich into king.
ciphers.hint: A small crunchy red root with a peppery bite.

poem_stanzas:
A cousin of the carrot, pale and cream,
I bide all winter in the frozen ground,
Cold makes me sweet, though sweetness was a dream,
And in the roasting pan I am found.

On Sunday tables next to beef I lie,
A homely root that many overlook,
The winter frost will sweeten me, and I
Am eaten from a well-worn country cook.
ciphers.hint: A pale sweet root, like a carrot but cream-colored.

poem_stanzas:
I am a fan of dark green crinkled leaves,
That shrink to a small spoonful when they stew,
A sailor's cartoon strength the world believes,
And farmers sow me when the winter's through.

For those who need green strength I am the spring,
A leafy iron for the blood and bone,
And children push me round the plate and sing
A song of protest in a mournful tone.
ciphers.hint: A dark leafy green that makes Popeye strong.

poem_stanzas:
I am a little forest on a stalk,
A green umbrella of a thousand trees,
I grow in cool and cloudy garden walk,
And shiver in the season's later breeze.

I was not loved by every child at first,
A green and bitter challenge on the plate,
But steam me tender, and the tide is reversed,
And even fussy eaters clean their slate.
ciphers.hint: A green vegetable shaped like a little tree.

poem_stanzas:
I come in green and long and slender form,
A summer squash that swells while you're away,
I hide beneath a giant leaf from storm,
And double size within a single day.

Exhausted gardeners will leave a pile
Of me upon a neighbor's porch and run,
I bake into a bread that makes them smile,
And still there will be more when day is done.
ciphers.hint: A long green summer squash that grows overnight.

poem_stanzas:
A tiny coin of earth, a flattened seed,
That swells in water and becomes a meal,
I feed the humble household in its need,
And make a hearty soup that poor men feel.

From ancient fields of Egypt and of Rome,
I travel in a sack to fill a pot,
My shape is like a lens inside the home,
And thickens winter soup when it is hot.
ciphers.hint: A tiny flat seed cooked in soups and stews.

poem_stanzas:
I am a golden smooth and spoonable cream,
That wobbles gently on a saucer's rim,
I crown a pudding in a yellow stream,
And sweeten holidays with eager vim.

On winter tables I am spooned for all,
A dust of nutmeg settles on my skin,
A gentle blanket after dinner's call,
A comfort that the sweetest spoons begin.
ciphers.hint: A soft, sweet yellow dessert made of milk and eggs.

poem_stanzas:
A slender bridge of earth between two seas,
So thin the ships must take the longer road,
Two continents are linked by such as these,
And armies cross where water nearly flowed.

A canal was carved through me to join two seas,
Two oceans met when diggers cut my clay,
A narrow neck that lets the ships go free,
And shortens half the voyages of the day.
ciphers.hint: A narrow strip of land connecting two larger landmasses.

poem_stanzas:
A narrow gash that running water scored,
With walls that climb on either side in shade,
A hidden cleft where only water roared,
A trench the patient river slowly made.

A line too small to locate on a chart,
A place where climbers scramble to descend,
I hold the runoff of a mountain's heart,
And down my throat the flash floods slowly bend.
ciphers.hint: A deep, narrow gorge worn by running water.

poem_stanzas:
A purple waste of heather, wide and bare,
Where mist descends and lonely curlews cry,
A land of broken stone and open air,
Where only hardy sheep and grouse can lie.

Romances set their brooding dramas here,
A treacherous bog can swallow up a path,
I am the wind and emptiness and fear,
And all the lonely beauty aftermath.
ciphers.hint: An open, rough, poorly drained upland of heather and grass.

poem_stanzas:
I am an open stretch of purple bloom,
Where no tall tree will stand upon the soil,
A sandy, sunlit, bee-loud kind of room,
Where heather roots and windswept grasses coil.

The adder and the deer both share my land,
A common and a golf course bear my name,
The hiker crosses with a map in hand,
And here a fictional villain staked a claim.
ciphers.hint: An open area of low shrubs, especially heather.

poem_stanzas:
A rounded hump upon a gentle plain,
A little swell the glacier left behind,
A place to sit and watch the clouds and rain,
And let the long grass whistle in the wind.

A word of Old and Middle English birth,
A gentle rise is all my modest plea,
A grassy bump upon the tumps of earth,
A place where sheep can stand and watch the sea.
ciphers.hint: A small, low, rounded hill.

poem_stanzas:
I am a rounded heap of earth or stone,
A little hill on flat or marshy ground,
The pitcher's rubber rests on me alone,
And buried kings beneath me may be found.

An ant will raise me, and a mole will too,
A baseball pitcher stands upon my back,
A mountain is a giant version of me,
And ancient graves lie underneath my track.
ciphers.hint: A raised hill or heap, often of earth.

poem_stanzas:
A narrow spine of stone that splits the sky,
The line where two descending slopes have met,
A walker follows up and climbs so high,
And sees two valleys from my silhouette.

A plough will turn me in a field of loam,
A line of pressure on a weather chart,
I am the roof line of a mountain home,
And where the rains divide and part.
ciphers.hint: A long narrow raised crest of land or a mountain top line.

poem_stanzas:
A narrow arm the ocean sends ashore,
A finger of the tide that feels the land,
A sheltered cove where little waves explore,
And boats may hide from storms on either hand.

A bay is wider, and a fjord is steep,
I am the modest opening between,
A place where sheltered fishing boats may sleep,
A quiet cleft where land and sea convene.
ciphers.hint: A small arm of water reaching into the land.

poem_stanzas:
A slender pipe of dark and polished wood,
I speak through two thin reeds that pinch and sing,
An orchestra will tune to me for good,
And to my note the strings and horns will ring.

The duck's lament, the swan's soft final call,
The shepherd's voice in many a country score,
I am the pensive reed within the hall,
The plaintive note that opens childhood's door.
ciphers.hint: A slender double-reed woodwind with a plaintive tone.

poem_stanzas:
I am the deepest voice of any band,
A brass and coiling serpent on the knee,
I hold the bottom end with heavy hand,
And anchor all the march and melody.

My mouthpiece is the widest of the brass,
My notes are round and slow and seldom high,
Beneath the oompah beat I help it pass,
And carry all the bass that shakes the sky.
ciphers.hint: The largest, lowest brass instrument.

poem_stanzas:
A slender tube of high and piercing note,
I lead the marching column with my breath,
My cousin is the flute in a long coat,
And I have cheered a march to life from death.

A drum will keep me company in line,
A piccolo and I are close in blood,
I fit a palm and by a wrist design,
And cheer a village fair through rain and mud.
ciphers.hint: A small high-pitched flute used with drums in marching.

poem_stanzas:
A tortoise shell once served me as a frame,
Two curving horns with strings stretched in between,
The singer plucked me as he praised a name,
And music rose where mourning had just been.

Apollo taught its use to mortal hands,
It walked with poets down the classic years,
It stands for lyric verse in many lands,
And shares its shape with quiet, heavenly spheres.
ciphers.hint: An ancient stringed instrument played by poets.

poem_stanzas:
A piece in parts, a journey with three stops,
A first that states, a slow one that may sing,
A final that returns and turns and drops,
A conversation with no words to bring.

The classical composers shaped my form,
For keyboard or for violin or reed,
I am a little drama, quiet or storm,
A wordless argument that players read.
ciphers.hint: A multi-movement instrumental work, often for piano or solo.

poem_stanzas:
I am the settling of a wandering line,
The fall that tells the ear a phrase is through,
The comfortable close, the final sign,
The point where resolutions come in view.

A full one rests and seals the homeward key,
A half still hangs a question in the air,
A plagal one comes down so quietly,
And marching feet will find me everywhere.
ciphers.hint: The closing sequence of chords that ends a phrase.

poem_stanzas:
Above the waist a man, below a goat,
With pointed ears and horns and shaggy thighs,
I play a reedy pipe in woodland note,
And chase the fleeing nymph with greedy eyes.

I follow Dionysus in his train,
A wild and wine-soaked reveler at his side,
I am the forest's mischief and its bane,
And through me all the ancient wildwoods ride.
ciphers.hint: A woodland creature, half man and half goat.

poem_stanzas:
A horse with feathered pinions, born of blood,
Who sprang from where a severed neck had bled,
I strike a spring from stone in a green wood,
And carry heroes where no road is led.

A rider urged me up to slay a beast,
A poet rode me to the sacred hill,
I serve the thunder's master at his feast,
And must be caught with bridle and with will.
ciphers.hint: The winged horse of Greek myth.

poem_stanzas:
Upon a rock I sing a honeyed song,
That lures the sailor from his steady track,
My voice is sweet, my purpose is the wrong,
And ships have broken on my singing back.

One hero filled his sailors' ears with wax,
And bound himself to listen and to live,
He learned how close my honeyed music tracks,
And steered away from all I had to give.
ciphers.hint: A creature whose singing lured sailors to their doom.

poem_stanzas:
I live beneath a bridge or in a hill,
A grumpy, hulking giant of the north,
At night I hoard my gold and keep quite still,
By day I turn to stone and venture forth.

Three billy goats once crossed my bridge and won,
And I was thrown into the river's foam,
A child may find me in the tale of fun,
And in the comments of the internet home.
ciphers.hint: A cave-dwelling giant of northern folklore, or a bridge toll-keeper.

poem_stanzas:
A tiny spirit of the air and brook,
A playful flicker in the forest shade,
I dance on dew and vanish with a look,
And leave a ring of mushrooms where I played.

A pixel figure borrows my small name,
A lively thing that flits across a screen,
A fairy-ring and I are much the same,
And both are gone as soon as they are seen.
ciphers.hint: A small, mischievous fairy spirit.

poem_stanzas:
I live and die within a single tree,
My life is bound to bark and leaf and root,
When it is felled, I fade to memory,
And nothing of me leaves a branch or shoot.

An oak or olive is my only home,
A Greek once feared to fell a sacred grove,
I am the spirit of the wooded dome,
And with my tree I live and breathe and love.
ciphers.hint: A tree spirit of Greek myth.

poem_stanzas:
I am the softening after winter's freeze,
The dripping from the eaves at noon's first touch,
The loosening of rivers by degrees,
And mud that smells of spring and means so much.

A frozen pond becomes a sheet of slush,
A buried bulb will lift a weary head,
The garden wakes from its long frozen hush,
And every stream is finding its old bed.
ciphers.hint: The melting of snow and ice as warmth returns.

poem_stanzas:
I am a wind that has outgrown a breeze,
A roaring rush that bends the tallest oak,
I whip the waves and harry ships with ease,
And to a forest I am no kind joke.

A weather warning often bears my name,
A sailor watches for a lowering sky,
I am the punishment the winds became,
The fierce and roaring force that none deny.
ciphers.hint: A very strong wind.

poem_stanzas:
I am a sudden shove that comes and goes,
A single puff that snatches at your hat,
A little breath that lifts the dirt and blows,
And rattles every window where it sat.

A leaf will dance and then the air is still,
I come between the calms on blustery days,
A sail will fill and slacken on a hill,
And dust will settle after all my ways.
ciphers.hint: A sudden brief rush of wind.

poem_stanzas:
I am the rain that hardened on the way,
A rattling handful on the pane and roof,
A stinging grain that turns the pavement gray,
A brittle, bouncing, frozen kind of proof.

Beneath me roads become a skating rink,
I drum upon the windshield and the hood,
A winter blend that hovers on the brink
Of snow and rain, and neither, understood.
ciphers.hint: Frozen rain that falls as ice pellets.

poem_stanzas:
I am the sudden color of the year,
The petaled opening of a long wait,
The proof that all the growing time is here,
The beauty that the gardener cannot rate.

A rose will make a season of my name,
A cherry tree will bury streets in pink,
A gardener will coax me into flame,
And in a week I wither on the brink.
ciphers.hint: A flower, or the time a plant opens its flowers.

poem_stanzas:
A golden dust that rides upon the bee,
A grain of life that travels bloom to bloom,
A sneeze in spring for those who breathe in me,
A yellow coat that settles in a room.

A watery eye will redden at my drift,
The wind may carry me for miles and more,
I am the father of the orchard's gift,
The yellow promise at the flower's core.
ciphers.hint: The fine powder from flowers that fertilizes other flowers.

poem_stanzas:
A tiny green beginning from a bean,
That pushes up through soil to find the light,
A promise of the garden yet unseen,
The first green foot of many a summer's height.

On sandwiches and salads I am found,
The bean and Brussels are my leafy kin,
A child may grow me in a jar, around
A window sill, from seed that's kept within.
ciphers.hint: A tiny new shoot growing from a seed.

poem_stanzas:
I climb the wall and hold with tiny feet,
A dark green army scaling brick and stone,
I swallow fences where the gardens meet,
And make an old house feel less alone.

A college wall is famous for my spread,
A carol pairs my name with holly's red,
I cover ruins where the roof is dead,
And starve the wall that dares to be my bed.
ciphers.hint: A climbing evergreen vine that covers walls.

poem_stanzas:
I hold a flame inside a frame of tin,
A little window and a hoop of wire,
I light the road when all the dark is in,
And guide a walking figure through the mire.

A paper version floats on water's face,
A festival will launch me to the sky,
A red one swings above a doorway's space,
And hollow pumpkins borrow from my eye.
ciphers.hint: A portable light enclosed in a case with a handle.

poem_stanzas:
I am a vessel with a swinging ear,
That hangs upon a hook beside a well,
I carry water, sand, and paint, and beer,
And in a sandbox I am king as well.

A child upon the beach will fill me up,
A janitor will dip me with a mop,
I take the milk before the calf will sup,
And I have hit the bottom with a plop.
ciphers.hint: An open container with a handle, used to carry liquids.

poem_stanzas:
I am a weight upon a shaft of wood,
That drives a nail and shapes the glowing steel,
A blacksmith's partner, builder's livelihood,
The sudden bang that makes a finger feel.

A gavel in a courtroom is my kin,
A claw behind my head will pull the nail,
I drive the metal home and split the skin,
And ring the anvil with a steady flail.
ciphers.hint: A tool with a heavy head used to drive nails.

poem_stanzas:
A blade with a wooden handle for the hand,
A sculptor's partner when he strikes a block,
I carve the marble, working as was planned,
And knock the unwanted stone with steady knock.

With a mallet I am driven, never struck,
A carpenter will pair me with a plane,
I make the grooves where joints will turn and tuck,
And wake the shape that sleeps in wood and vein.
ciphers.hint: A tool with a sharp edge for carving wood or stone.

poem_stanzas:
I sit upon a stove and gather steam,
A spout that whistles when the water boils,
I am the kitchen's warm and homely dream,
That fills a winter morning with my toils.

When camping, I am hung above a fire,
I pour the tea and steam the windowpane,
I whistle when the water climbs the wire,
And call the household to the table again.
ciphers.hint: A metal pot with a spout for boiling water.

poem_stanzas:
A blade both short and sharp for close at hand,
With edge and point and hilt for gripping tight,
A weapon hidden in a cloak or band,
A sudden glint that wakes the dark of night.

A Roman in the forum felt my sting,
A hidden hand could end a sleep or throne,
The word for me is used to mean a thing
That cuts a friendship to the very bone.
ciphers.hint: A short pointed knife used as a weapon.

poem_stanzas:
I ride upon the shoulder or the back,
A tube of leather or of painted wood,
I hold the slender shafts that never lack,
And keep the archer's deadly arrows good.

The same small word can mean to shake with fear,
So archers carry me and tremble too,
A hunter's gear for hunting fallow deer,
A bundle full of feathered sticks in view.
ciphers.hint: A case slung on the back to hold an archer's arrows.

poem_stanzas:
I sit upon a horse and take the weight,
A padded perch of leather and of steel,
I make the rider comfortable and straight,
And ease the long day's muscle and its feel.

A cowboy straps me on and rides away,
A stirrup dangles down on either side,
A bike and truck have borrowed me today,
And all my purpose is to give a ride.
ciphers.hint: A leather seat strapped on a horse for a rider.

poem_stanzas:
I have no charge, I sit within the core,
Beside a positive companion, bound,
Without me many atoms are no more,
And isotopes are made where I am found.

I split a heavy nucleus in two,
And loosed a power the world has feared and used,
A star that turns to one of me will strew
A pulse of light that sky-watchers have mused.
ciphers.hint: A neutral particle found in the nucleus of an atom.

poem_stanzas:
I carry positive within the core,
The count of me decides what element,
I sit with a companion and explore
The metal's name and all its ornament.

A giant accelerator will speed me fast,
Two hydrogen are made to race and meet,
A collider has studied me at last,
And found a host of particles more fleet.
ciphers.hint: A positively charged particle in an atom's nucleus.

poem_stanzas:
I am the pressure in an unseen stream,
The shove that sets the electrons on their way,
I come from cells and lightning and from steam,
And I am what the transformer must obey.

A bolt of lightning carries me in full,
A household socket holds a steady share,
A multimeter will read my pull,
And bulbs will brighten by the strength I bear.
ciphers.hint: The electrical pressure that pushes current through a wire.

poem_stanzas:
A ring of wire that must not break or gap,
The journey of a current out and back,
A broken one will blow a fuse's trap,
And leave a room in unforeseen attack.

On tracks a driver makes me many laps,
A breaker opens when the current spikes,
A logic board is full of me and maps,
And every charge must travel where I like.
ciphers.hint: A complete loop through which electricity flows.

poem_stanzas:
I am a folded chain that acts as a key,
I fit a shape and hurry it along,
Without me, all the body's chemistry
Would slow to nothing and the cells grow wrong.

I dwell in stomach, laundry soap, and seed,
My name will often end in a set of sounds,
I speed a chemical with no need
Of heat, and life on me in part abounds.
ciphers.hint: A protein that speeds up chemical reactions in living things.

poem_stanzas:
I am the drift of everything toward mess,
The reason time has only one direction,
The reason heat will scatter and digress,
And nothing ever ends in true perfection.

A broken cup will never mend alone,
A tidy room will slowly fall apart,
A physicist will find me in the drone
Of every engine, every human heart.
ciphers.hint: A measure of disorder; the tendency toward decay.

poem_stanzas:
Upon a lawn of summer I am played,
A wooden mallet strikes a painted ball,
Through little hoops a crooked path is laid,
And everyone must wait and take their call.

A flamingo was the mallet in a dream,
A hedgehog served as ball in Wonderland,
A gentle summer game of distant aim,
That ends with tea and a congratulating hand.
ciphers.hint: A lawn game played by hitting balls through hoops with mallets.

poem_stanzas:
I face the stern and pull with back and arm,
A sliding seat goes forward and retreats,
A rhythm that a crew must keep from harm,
A steely stroke that every oarsman beats.

An eight will fly with one and eight and cox,
A river race is where my speed is shown,
Two blades will bite the water's glassy locks,
And leave a trail of arrow heads alone.
ciphers.hint: Pulling oars to propel a boat.

poem_stanzas:
A spear of metal balanced in the palm,
I fly across the field in a long arc,
A running throw that keeps the shoulder calm,
And lands a point beyond the farthest mark.

An ancient warrior carried me to war,
An athlete now will hurl me for a prize,
I spin and slice the air and then I score,
A single tip that heaven-reaching flies.
ciphers.hint: A spear thrown as far as possible for distance.

poem_stanzas:
A row of wooden frames across the track,
That must be cleared with neither touch nor fall,
A rhythm of a leap and landing back,
A test of speed and nerve above them all.

An athlete's stride is counted to my beat,
A horse will clear me in a jumping course,
A life is full of me on every street,
And few approach me without some remorse.
ciphers.hint: Barriers a runner must leap over in a race.

poem_stanzas:
A flat and heavy plate of stone or steel,
That spins from out a circle on the ground,
A thrower whirls and lets the weight reveal,
The farthest arc that any arm has found.

A famous statue holds me in his hand,
An ancient game of Greece still sends me far,
I whirl and sail and settle in the sand,
A flattened sun that leaves a dusty scar.
ciphers.hint: A heavy flat disc thrown for distance.

poem_stanzas:
A game of mud and muscle and an egg,
Where hands will throw and feet will punt and run,
A scrum of giants shoving leg to leg,
A try that ends with all the fever done.

A school once picked the ball up from the ground,
And made a game of running with the thing,
The ball is oval, brown, and leather-bound,
And every player wears a mouthguard ring.
ciphers.hint: A team game with an oval ball, carrying and tackling.
